title: Linked lists
objective: Follow next pointers, and reverse a list by turning each arrow around.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): linked lists

simplifies: A singly linked list is shown. Real code also handles an empty list (head is None), which this function already does: the loop never runs.

quiz.prompt: Getting the 500th node of a linked list takes…

options.explanation: Only arrays can jump to an index. A list has to be followed node by node.

options.text: About 500 steps, following next from the head
options.explanation: Right. That is the trade-off: lists insert anywhere cheaply, but reach items slowly.

options.text: It depends on the value stored
options.explanation: Position, not value, decides how far you walk.

quiz.prompt: Why save nxt before changing cur.next?

options.text: Otherwise the rest of the list is lost
options.explanation: Right. Once cur.next points back, nothing else remembers where the old next node was.
It is about correctness, not speed.
Python allows either order; only one order works.
